informational_independence.scope: Independent external reliability and maintainability engineering research corpus.

population.stop_rule: Saturation/evidence-completeness reached: additional searches would refine attribution or examples but did not reveal a distinct property family or alter a trigger, cheap path, precondition, mature form or disposition.

syntax_only_normalisation: JSON key ordering, Markdown escaping, UTF-8/LF output and deterministic ZIP metadata only; no frozen research content was reopened or revised during packaging.

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Explicit required-function and mission semantics
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Wartime/post-war equipment reliability requirements; mission-success language in military reliability programmes; later dependability standards.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: State a numerical reliability objective for an item over a mission time.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A probability has no engineering meaning until the required function, consumer, conditions, interval and failure threshold are fixed.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: The named system or service function must meet specified performance, timing, state and consequence criteria for the declared consumer.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Failure is non-performance, untimely performance, erroneous performance or performance below the declared threshold—not merely component death.
properties.MECHANISM: Define function, mission/service, modes, performance thresholds, failure scoring, consumer and mission time/demand before modelling or testing.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any reliability, availability, demonstration, redundancy, recovery or service-level claim that could drive design, release, maintenance or acceptance.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low-consequence reversible work, use a direct pass/fail functional check and a short observation window rather than a probabilistic programme.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stakeholder/consumer criteria, mission phases, state authority, measurable outputs and an agreed scoring rule.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents metric optimisation for a component or proxy while the actual mission/user function fails.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Mission owner, service consumer, operator, maintainer, acceptance authority or risk decision-maker.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Ambiguous verbs; moving thresholds; component-centric scoring; omitted partial failures; disputed responsibility boundaries.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Requirements can be bureaucratic or falsely precise; rare severe consequences can be hidden by an average success definition.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Component survival targets were broadened to mission reliability, functional failure, user journeys and consequence-aware degraded states.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A testable, versioned mission contract that binds required function, mode, profile, environment, interval/demand, degraded acceptance and consumer consequence.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A reliability requirement template is optional; the property is semantic closure on what success and failure mean.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: AWS, Meta and GitLab incidents show that locally alive components can coexist with unavailable or incorrect end functions (SRC-058–SRC-060).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: No evidence supports a context-free scalar called “reliability” independent of function, conditions and time/demand.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should multi-consumer missions aggregate conflicting thresholds without erasing vulnerable or high-consequence users?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Operational-profile, environment and demand definition
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Life testing and field-data stratification; software operational-profile work in the early 1990s; modern service and mission profiling.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Estimate reliability under a specified duty cycle and environment or sample test operations in field-frequency proportion.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Failure probability changes with usage, load, environment, mode, maintenance, software inputs and dependencies.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: The function in ERM-P001 under the actual or deliberately bounded distribution of demands and conditions.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Evidence or design appears reliable under a convenient profile but fails under real frequency, severity, mode transition or rare consequence-important demand.
properties.MECHANISM: Version and measure workloads, mission phases, physical stresses, user classes, duty cycles, dependencies, maintenance states and rare critical operations.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Prediction, demonstration, accelerated testing, software testing, SLO definition, capacity planning, maintenance policy or field-transfer claim.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Use a small set of bounding scenarios when a full probability distribution would not change the decision.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Telemetry or credible mission analysis, stable definitions, sampling weights and explicit treatment of rare high-consequence demands.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces false confidence from laboratory, average-load or dominant-user evidence that excludes the conditions causing failure.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Test planner, reliability analyst, service owner, maintainer, release authority and mission decision-maker.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Stale profiles; survivorship bias; request-weighting that hides users; omitted maintenance/change states; extrapolation beyond observed support.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Profiles can encode current behaviour and suppress novel uses; high-consequence rare events may deserve more weight than frequency implies.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Frequency-only profiles evolved toward stratified, consequence-aware and continuously refreshed exposure models.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A configuration-bound, uncertainty-labelled exposure model that supports both representative sampling and explicit stress/boundary cases.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A workload spreadsheet is optional; the property is evidence about where, how often and under what conditions function is demanded.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Outage accounts show recovery and load behaviour outside routinely exercised profiles, including full subsystem restart and global-backbone loss (SRC-058, SRC-059).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: No fixed profile remains valid after material product, dependency, user or mission change.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should profiles combine frequency, severity and epistemic novelty without becoming too expensive to maintain?

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CLAIM: A configuration-bound, uncertainty-labelled exposure model that supports both representative sampling and explicit stress/boundary cases.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR: Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Exact hardware, software, data, model, dependency and procedure versions.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN: Predeclared sampling/censoring, failure scoring, exposure and stopping rules.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MODEL: Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.ASSUMPTIONS: Independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage and representativeness are explicit.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY: Intervals, posterior uncertainty or bounded qualitative confidence; point estimates alone are insufficient.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS: Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.COVERAGE: Claim coverage is limited to tested/observed failure modes, environments and paths.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Test planner, reliability analyst, service owner, maintainer, release authority and mission decision-maker.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS: Evidence expires when configuration, profile, environment, support organisation or dependencies materially change.

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Explicit complete, partial, intermittent, latent and degraded failure states
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: FMEA/FMECA failure-mode taxonomies, multi-state reliability, maintainability and dependable-computing fault/error/failure distinctions.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Classify each item as operating or failed and enumerate failure modes.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Binary up/down states erase partial service, false output, intermittency, dormant standby defects and acceptable degradation.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Required function and quality thresholds for each operating mode, including which reduced capabilities remain acceptable and for how long.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: A harmful state is classified as “up,” or an acceptable degraded state is counted as complete failure, corrupting decisions and metrics.
properties.MECHANISM: Define state space, observable criteria, transitions, dwell limits, latent conditions, false indications and consumer consequences.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Systems with multiple modes, redundancy, standby, partial service, performance thresholds, intermittent faults or hidden protective functions.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A binary state is sufficient only when the consumer consequence is genuinely binary and the observation tests the complete function.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: State observability, mission criteria, transition rules, timing and authority for accepting/ending degradation.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Enables meaningful availability, diagnostics, degradation and recovery claims instead of uptime theatre.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Operator, mission owner, service consumer, model builder and incident reviewer.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: State explosion; inconsistent scoring; unobservable latent states; “degraded” used to normalise unacceptable service.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Multi-state models can create false precision and obscure simpler decisive thresholds.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Binary life models were supplemented by functional failure, multi-state availability, degraded modes and user-impact measures.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A minimal consequence-relevant state model with explicit observation, entry/exit criteria, allowed duration and treatment of latent states.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A state diagram is optional; the property is unambiguous classification of the states that matter to the mission.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: GitLab’s service was unavailable and lost data while different storage functions had different outcomes; Meta’s DNS servers were locally operational but unreachable (SRC-059, SRC-060).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: No single multi-state taxonomy transfers without mission-specific thresholds.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What is the minimum state resolution that preserves consequence without making evidence collection intractable?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: System boundary and failure-attribution discipline
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Fault-tree ground rules, RBD success paths, field failure reporting and service dependency analysis.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Choose the item under analysis and attribute each observed failure to a component.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Changing the item boundary or excluding dependencies, maintenance, planned windows or user-side effects can manufacture reliability.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: The end-to-end function across all components, services, people and support resources inside the declared responsibility/decision boundary.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: A mission failure is omitted, double-counted or assigned to an external party so that no owner sees the actual system risk.
properties.MECHANISM: Declare analysis boundary, inclusions/exclusions, interfaces, responsibility versus causal attribution, denominator and disputed cases.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: RBD/FTA/FMEA, SLA/SLO, supplier reliability, incident metrics, field-return analysis or cross-organisation service paths.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a local reversible decision, state a narrow boundary explicitly and avoid claiming end-to-end reliability.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Dependency inventory, interface contracts, event correlation, shared clocks/identifiers and adjudication rules.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents local optimisation and denominator gaming while preserving causal learning across interfaces.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: System owner, supplier manager, SRE/service owner, maintainer and acceptance authority.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Boundary disputes; “external cause” exclusion; planned-maintenance exclusions; missing user telemetry; ownership confused with causation.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Very broad boundaries make measurement and accountability difficult; too-narrow boundaries make claims irrelevant.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Component attribution evolved toward end-to-end dependency and consumer-consequence accounting while retaining local causal analysis.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A layered boundary model: end-to-end consequence for reliability claims, plus component/dependency attribution for corrective action.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A service map or fault tree is optional; the property is stable scope and transparent exclusions.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: AWS and Meta postmortems show that a shared storage, backbone, DNS or control dependency can dominate many nominally separate services (SRC-058, SRC-059).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: No evidence supports treating contractual exclusion as physical independence.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should attribution metrics preserve both end-to-end accountability and non-blaming causal decomposition?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Separate reliability, availability, maintainability, supportability and durability claims
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Post-war reliability/maintainability programmes, repairable-system probability, logistics support and current IEC dependability vocabulary.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Report MTBF, MTTR and availability as related but distinct quantities.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: High availability can result from frequent fast repairs; high reliability can coexist with slow repair; maintainable design can fail operationally for lack of support.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: A declared mission interval and restoration/support conditions for the item or service.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: A decision substitutes one RAM measure for another and accepts the wrong failure frequency, downtime, repair burden or life limitation.
properties.MECHANISM: Use distinct estimands and state models: no-failure probability, probability of being up, restoration-time distribution, support delay and life/degradation measures.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any claim using reliability, uptime, availability, MTBF, MTTR, serviceability, durability or operational readiness.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Use direct failure count and downtime decomposition when a full stochastic model is unnecessary; never collapse the labels.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Consistent clocks, failure/restoration definitions, exposure, repair-completion criteria and support-delay data.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Systematic failure-mode, effect and propagation challenge
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: 1949 military FMECA, later MIL-STD-1629A, FTA and current IEC 60812.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Enumerate component failure modes and document local, next-higher and end effects in a worksheet.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Nominal architecture descriptions do not reveal plausible loss, erroneous output, timing, interface or propagation paths.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: The function and boundary defined by ERM-P001–P004.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: A plausible mode or propagation path remains uncontrolled because analysis stopped at a component label or single failure.
properties.MECHANISM: Challenge functions and interfaces with plausible modes; trace local-to-end effects, controls, detectability, combinations and evidence for treatment.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Novel/high-consequence functions, complex interfaces, weak field history, design change, repeated incidents or uncertain propagation.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Use a focused “what can fail and what happens next?” review for simple reversible systems; do not require a full worksheet.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Current architecture/configuration, knowledgeable cross-functional participants, explicit ground rules and closure evidence.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Finds single points, latent paths, missing diagnostics and consequence escalation early enough to change design or test.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Designer, reliability engineer, maintainer, tester, operator and acceptance authority.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Checklist copying; unbounded rows; subjective ranks; omission of software/human/dependent combinations; controls listed but unverified.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Bottom-up FMEA can miss interactions and multiple failures; FTA can inherit an incomplete top event and independence assumptions.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Worksheet-centric analysis evolved toward functional, interface, dynamic, dependency and evidence-linked analysis chosen by question.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A proportionate, configuration-bound adversarial analysis that links each important failure path to prevention, detection, containment, recovery or accepted residual risk.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The FMEA/FMECA table is not the property; systematic challenge and verified closure are.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Major outages repeatedly involve coupled operations, dependencies and recovery paths that a part-only checklist would miss (SRC-058–SRC-062).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: No method is complete for unknown failure modes or all combinations; analysis must be tested and refreshed.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can dynamic/software interactions be covered without producing unreviewable model size?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Single-point and latent-failure exposure control
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: FMECA critical-item lists, fault trees, standby-system analysis and built-in test.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Identify any single item whose failure causes mission loss and any dormant protective item whose failure is hidden.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A nominally protected system can have a hidden one-shot failure at a switch, sensor, shared utility, standby channel or maintenance state.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Specified fault tolerance or degraded mission capability under the declared initiating fault set.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: One fault, or one fault plus an undetected latent condition, defeats required function.
properties.MECHANISM: Identify cut sets and latent protective failures; eliminate, isolate, monitor or periodically proof-test them; bound exposure time.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Redundancy, standby, protective functions, emergency equipment, rarely demanded recovery paths and maintenance bypasses.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For simple systems, trace the end-to-end path once and directly exercise the spare/protective function rather than build a full quantitative tree.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Complete boundary, realistic initial state, demand rate, proof-test interval, detection coverage and restoration plan.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: Credible failure-domain independence, common-cause analysis, standby condition, switchover coverage and state compatibility.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents false redundancy and limits time spent unknowingly one fault away from mission loss.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architect, maintainer, operator, tester and mission-risk authority.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Hidden bypasses; common sensor/switch; proof test that does not test the whole path; maintenance disables both channels; dormant ageing.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: “Single failure” focus can distract from correlated multi-fault and systemic conditions.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Static single-point lists evolved to minimal cut sets, latent-exposure intervals, dynamic standby and common-cause analysis.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Explicit minimal failure sets including latent states, with elimination or tested detection/repair intervals matched to consequence.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A critical-items list is optional; the property is actual removal or bounded exposure of decisive failure sets.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: GitLab’s failed backup/replication paths and Meta’s simultaneous loss of normal and out-of-band access demonstrate latent and shared recovery-path exposure (SRC-059, SRC-060).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: A zero single-point-failure count does not prove resilience to dependent combinations.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should latent exposure be prioritised when proof testing itself creates maintenance risk?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Common-cause, common-mode and correlated-dependency analysis
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Nuclear and aerospace common-cause analysis, diversity debates, multiversion software experiments and cloud dependency failures.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Apply a beta factor or common-cause event category to redundant components.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Nominal parallel paths share specification, design, environment, power, control, state, supplier, maintenance, deployment or operator causes.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Continued or degraded required function after the claimed fault set.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Several “independent” elements fail together or sequentially from a shared coupling, invalidating the parallel reliability calculation.
properties.MECHANISM: Enumerate failure domains and coupling factors; seek empirical CCF data; model dependence; separate shared controls; test correlated scenarios; reduce concentration.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any redundancy, multi-region, multi-vendor, diverse implementation, backup, standby or third-party dependency claim.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: When independence cannot be supported, treat copies as one failure domain for the decision and avoid precision theatre.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Architecture/dependency visibility, configuration/supplier data, incident linkage and credible dependence parameters or conservative bounds.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: Credible failure-domain independence, common-cause analysis, standby condition, switchover coverage and state compatibility.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Avoids orders-of-magnitude overstatement of redundancy benefit and exposes hidden ecosystem concentration.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architect, reliability modeller, service owner, procurement/supplier manager and mission-risk authority.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Unobserved coupling; common specification; shared update; shared operator; correlated maintenance; regional/control-plane dependence; sparse CCF data.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: CCF parameters are uncertain and domain-specific; pessimistic bounding can erase economically useful redundancy.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Assumed independence evolved to explicit failure-domain, beta/alpha-factor, diversity and correlated-dependency treatment.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A qualitative-plus-quantitative coupling argument that states what is shared, what is separated, the evidence for residual dependence and consequences if the assumption fails.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A “multi-AZ” label or beta-factor entry is not the property; credible domain separation and dependence evidence are.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Meta’s backbone/DNS/tool coupling, AWS’s S3 dependency fan-out and CrowdStrike’s homogeneous update propagation provide direct incident support (SRC-058, SRC-059, SRC-061, SRC-062).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Redundancy still pays when failure domains and transfer paths are credibly separated; the criticism is of assumed independence, not redundancy itself.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can dependence be bounded in rapidly changing service ecosystems with sparse joint-failure observations?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Redundancy only with credible independence, coverage and switchover
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Voting and standby reliability, von Neumann’s unreliable-component constructions, aerospace fault tolerance and high-availability failover.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Place independent parallel components in an RBD or vote among replicas to multiply down failure probability.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Copy count is mistaken for fault tolerance while detection, standby health, transfer logic, state and common causes remain unproven.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Full or declared degraded mission function after the fault class and within the transfer deadline.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Both paths fail together, the spare is latent-bad, switchover does not occur, transfer corrupts state, capacity is insufficient or adjudication selects the wrong output.
properties.MECHANISM: Specify tolerated faults; isolate domains; monitor standby; validate detection/decision/transfer/state/capacity; test under representative load and failed-control conditions.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: N+1/N+2, TMR, replicas, active-active, hot/warm/cold standby, alternate path, multi-region or recovery-block claim.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Prefer one simple, observable system or a manual spare when added redundancy creates more coupling than risk reduction.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: ERM-P008 common-cause analysis, diagnostic coverage, switchover reliability, compatible state, spare capacity and maintainable configuration.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: Credible failure-domain independence, common-cause analysis, standby condition, switchover coverage and state compatibility.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Provides continuity or bounded degradation for credible fault classes without converting diagrams into false assurance.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architect, operator, mission owner and acceptance authority.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Voter/switch single point; dormant spare; split brain; stale state; overload after failover; simultaneous maintenance; common update/specification.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Redundancy adds components, interfaces, operational modes and maintenance burden; diversity can impair maintainability.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Simple parallel blocks evolved to coverage-aware, state-aware and failure-domain-aware fault tolerance.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A fault-tolerance claim stated as tolerated fault set × coverage × independence × transfer/state/capacity evidence, with residual common-cause risk.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A redundancy diagram is optional; the property is an evidenced alternate path that actually assumes the mission.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: GitLab’s nominal standby and backup paths were not usable as assumed; AWS recovery showed restart scale and capacity safeguards mattered (SRC-058, SRC-060).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Under validated independence and coverage, mathematical and field evidence strongly support redundancy for specified faults.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What minimum evidence justifies numerical independence rather than a conservative correlated model?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Fault containment regions and propagation barriers
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Hardware isolation and protection, recovery blocks, fault-containment regions, partitioning/cells and blast-radius engineering.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Physically or logically isolate faults so they cannot cross a defined region.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A local defect, overload, bad update or repair action propagates into a system-wide outage or corrupts recovery sources.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Critical function remains available, degrades within criteria or can be restored without contamination beyond the region.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Shared state, control, resource pools, retries, maintenance or deployment bypass the intended boundary.
properties.MECHANISM: Partition state/resources/control; enforce quotas and circuit boundaries; stage deployment; isolate maintenance; define escape paths; test boundary breach.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: High fan-out dependencies, untrusted/rapid changes, fault tolerance, multi-tenant resources, recovery sources and high-consequence functions.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Use simple rate limits, manual change gates or one-way isolation when full cell architecture is disproportionate.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Known propagation mechanisms, independent controls, observability at boundaries and recovery capacity outside the failed region.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: Credible failure-domain independence, common-cause analysis, standby condition, switchover coverage and state compatibility.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Limits blast radius, preserves diagnostic evidence and leaves unaffected capacity for recovery.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architect, operator, incident commander, maintainer and mission owner.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Control plane shared by all cells; global configuration; retry storms; corrupt replicated state; operator/tool privileges cross boundaries.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Partitioning increases cost, consistency and operational complexity; false isolation can hide accumulating latent faults.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Physical isolation broadened to software cells, staged rollout, resource isolation, state quarantine and organisational blast-radius controls.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A tested containment argument covering state, control, resources, dependencies, maintenance and recovery—not merely data-plane topology.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A cell diagram or “bulkhead” label is optional; the property is measured containment of specified propagation.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: AWS explicitly identified cell partitioning and safer capacity-removal controls after the 2017 S3 event (SRC-058).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Containment cannot eliminate shared specification, governance or supply-chain common causes by itself.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should containment be measured for semantic corruption that crosses otherwise isolated replicas?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Fault detection coverage tied to required function
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Built-in test, fault coverage in fault-tolerant systems, model-based residuals and service monitoring.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Assign a coverage probability that a component fault is detected and correctly handled.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Nominal reliability or redundancy assumes faults are noticed before propagation or before a standby demand, but monitoring sees only a subset.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Timely recognition that the required function or a protective/recovery path has entered a defined failed/degraded state.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: A green component signal coexists with broken end-to-end function, or the target fault is outside the monitor’s coverage.
properties.MECHANISM: Define the fault/failure population; map each to observables and latency; measure misses/false alarms; include end-to-end functional probes and dormant paths.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Automatic failover, latent protective functions, remote operation, SLO alerting, PHM or any claim using “coverage.”
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A direct manual functional test may dominate elaborate monitoring for infrequent, low-cost, reversible decisions.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Observable consequences, representative fault injection/field labels, threshold calibration, independent monitoring dependencies and action path.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Turns “health” from a heartbeat into evidence that target failures are likely to be noticed in time.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Operator, maintainer, automated recovery controller and mission owner.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Silent semantic failure; monitor shares failed dependency; stale telemetry; test-mode-only coverage; false green after partial recovery.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Coverage numbers are often generated from an incomplete fault list and can be falsely precise.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: One-bit BIT and liveness evolved toward function-level, multi-signal and user-journey monitoring with explicit coverage gaps.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A coverage claim indexed by fault class, operating mode, latency and end-to-end consequence, validated independently of the monitored component.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A health dashboard is optional; the property is known detection performance over the relevant failure population.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Meta’s DNS servers were operational but unreachable; internal diagnostic tools were also lost, showing local health and diagnostic independence can both fail (SRC-059).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: No monitor can prove absence of unknown latent failures; claims must remain coverage-bounded.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can semantic/user-journey coverage be measured when ground truth is delayed or disputed?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Diagnostic isolation, ambiguity and confidence discipline
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Troubleshooting/testability, model-based diagnosis, ambiguity groups and PHM.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Localise a detected fault to a line-replaceable unit so maintenance can replace it.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: An alarm identifies a symptom but not the actionable cause, leading to wrong replacement, unsafe automation or long downtime.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Identify a cause set at the resolution needed for safe containment, repair or recovery within the mission deadline.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Premature root-cause certainty, unresolved ambiguity, confounded dependency symptoms or diagnosis drift triggers ineffective action.
properties.MECHANISM: Maintain hypotheses/ambiguity groups; seek discriminating observations; calibrate confidence; match action reversibility and authority to uncertainty.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Multiple plausible causes, costly/irreversible repair, automatic remediation, dependency failures or repeated “no fault found.”
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: When several causes share the same safe reversible remedy, act on the symptom and defer exact root cause.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Causal/functional model, sensor validity, fault labels, access to dependency state, time budget and action-cost model.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces parts-cannon maintenance, repeated restarts and harmful automation while improving restoration time.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Maintainer, operator, automated controller, incident commander and design owner.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Sensor fault mistaken for process fault; correlated symptoms; training/domain shift; confirmation bias; unavailable evidence during outage.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Root-cause analysis can become post-hoc narrative; exact isolation may cost more time than safe restoration permits.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Deterministic fault codes evolved toward probabilistic/model-based diagnosis with explicit ambiguity, confidence and decision coupling.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Decision-sufficient diagnosis: calibrated cause set, evidence, ambiguity, latency and reversible action—not forced single-cause certainty.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A root-cause label is not the property; discriminating evidence and action-relevant confidence are.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Large outages show diagnosis can be slowed because the same dependency failure removes normal tools or access (SRC-059).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: For simple deterministic faults, direct tests can establish cause cheaply; probabilistic diagnosis should not be mandatory.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should diagnosis confidence be calibrated for rare faults and changing configurations with sparse labels?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Explicit false-positive, false-negative and action cost
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Statistical detection theory, BIT false alarms, condition monitoring and modern alerting/anomaly detection.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Specify detection probability and false-alarm rate for a built-in test.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Increasing sensitivity can create maintenance-induced failures, alert fatigue or needless shutdown, while low sensitivity misses the recovery window.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: A monitoring/diagnostic decision that minimises mission-relevant expected loss under declared consequences and constraints.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: A threshold is selected from model accuracy alone without the cost of unnecessary action, delay, missed failure or operator saturation.
properties.MECHANISM: Estimate conditional errors by mode/profile; attach action/consequence costs; calibrate thresholds; monitor drift; permit abstention/manual review.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Anomaly detection, PHM, health checks, alerting, automatic failover/remediation or costly inspection/replacement.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Use a conservative rule or human confirmation when event rate is low and labels cannot support fine calibration.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Ground truth or adjudicated outcomes, base rates, representative profile, action-cost model and feedback after action.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents a superficially “accurate” detector from reducing total dependability.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Operator, maintainer, service owner and automated-action authority.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Base-rate neglect; threshold gaming; alert suppression; label leakage; false alarm causing invasive maintenance; missed latent fault.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Monetising severe consequences can be ethically or practically difficult; uncertain costs can create false optimisation.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Single sensitivity targets evolved toward calibrated trade-offs, precision/recall by consequence, abstention and human-in-the-loop action.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A decision-calibrated coverage argument with uncertainty, base rates, action costs, drift checks and safe fallback.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: An ROC/AUC chart or alert count is not the property; decision loss under the actual profile is.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Operational guidance and outage practice show that alerts must support action, not merely detect metric deviations; excessive or misleading signals can delay response.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Where a direct deterministic functional check exists, statistical threshold optimisation is unnecessary.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should rare catastrophic misses be represented when empirical frequency is too small for stable estimation?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Graceful degradation with explicit mission priorities
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Fail-soft/fail-operational computing, multi-state reliability, survivability and service load shedding.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Continue with reduced throughput or disabled noncritical functions after faults.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Binary shutdown wastes residual capability, but uncontrolled “keep running” can hide unsafe, corrupt or inequitable service.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Preserve prioritised critical function within degraded performance, time and consequence limits until repair/recovery or safe stop.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: The degraded state violates unstated dependencies, hides data loss, starves a user class, exceeds duration or cannot be exited.
properties.MECHANISM: Predefine capability tiers, priorities, admission/load shedding, observability, annunciation, time limits, exit/escalation and recovery tests.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Capacity loss, partial dependency failure, redundancy exhaustion or missions where some function is better than none.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Stop safely when degraded operation has no defensible acceptance criteria or adds greater consequence than interruption.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Mission prioritisation, state model, resource reservation, independent observability, operator/user communication and recovery path.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Converts residual resources into protected critical service while bounding hidden deterioration.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Mission owner, user populations, operator and incident commander.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Silent quality erosion; overload of remaining capacity; untested feature interactions; priority inversion; indefinite degraded mode.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: “Graceful” is value-laden; degradation may shift harm to less visible consumers or conflict with safety/security constraints.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Fail-soft hardware evolved toward mission-tiered service, load shedding, partial availability and explicit degraded-state SLOs.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A tested degradation contract specifying protected functions, sacrificed functions, consumer impact, observability, duration and exit criteria.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A feature flag or “degraded mode” label is not the property; controlled consequence and exit are.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: AWS restored APIs in stages and Meta carefully ramped traffic to avoid secondary overload, illustrating partial recovery and capacity-aware return (SRC-058, SRC-059).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: For some safety-, integrity- or security-critical functions, shutdown/containment is superior to continued degraded operation.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should fairness and vulnerable-user consequences be built into degraded-service priorities?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Contextual selection of fail-safe, fail-stop and fail-operational objectives
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Protective engineering, fail-stop computing, fail-operational aerospace/transport systems and high-availability services.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Choose either a safe state on failure or continued operation through redundancy.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: “Keep running” and “stop safely” protect different consequences and can conflict under uncertain state.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: The action after fault must minimise mission/consumer consequence under the applicable safety, integrity, availability and recoverability priorities.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: A universal availability objective continues corrupt/unsafe operation, or a universal stop policy destroys a time-critical mission that could tolerate degradation.
properties.MECHANISM: Perform consequence- and mode-specific objective selection; define trigger, authority, state confidence, tolerated duration and fallback.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Functions where interruption and continued erroneous operation have materially different consequences.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Default to a simple safe stop for reversible low-consequence work when continued correctness cannot be established.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Consequence model, state observability, independent protection, degraded criteria and cross-discipline constraints.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents reliability optimisation from overriding more important mission consequences.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Mission authority, operator, affected users and cross-functional assurance owners.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Ambiguous safe state; unsafe latent degradation; failover to corrupt state; emergency shutdown causes cascading loss.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: No reliability-only rule resolves the value trade-off; evidence from one domain cannot set another domain’s objective.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Binary slogans evolved toward mode- and consequence-specific state machines with fail-operational intervals and escalation to stop.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A source-grounded, explicitly prioritised transition policy rather than a generic “always available” or “always fail safe” rule.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A “fail-safe” label is not the property; the consequence-based transition and evidence are.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Meta’s staged restoration avoided a potentially destabilising immediate return, showing recovery action must consider secondary consequence (SRC-059).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Context determines which objective dominates; no general ranking was supported.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should authority be allocated when state confidence is low and safety, security and continuity owners disagree?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Recovery closes on required function and state postconditions
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Repairable-system restoration, recovery blocks, high-availability operations, recovery-oriented computing and modern reconstitution guidance.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Count repair complete when the failed component is returned to an “up” state.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Restart, failover or repair may leave stale/corrupt state, unavailable dependencies, insufficient capacity or the initiating common cause.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Re-establish the ERM-P001 required function, authoritative state and dependency readiness within the declared restoration bound.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Process starts but user/mission function is wrong, incomplete, too slow, unauthorised or vulnerable to immediate recurrence.
properties.MECHANISM: Define recovery source/authority, reconcile state, verify dependencies/capacity, perform independent end-to-end functional checks and control return to service.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Restart, retry, failover, rollback, restore, rebuild, repair, workaround or disaster recovery.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For stateless, low-consequence functions, a direct end-to-end transaction after restart may be sufficient.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Valid source, diagnosis/containment, state semantics, acceptance criteria, independent observability and fallback.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents “green after restart” from being mistaken for restoration and reduces recurrent/corrupt recovery.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Operator, incident commander, mission owner, user and return-to-service authority.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Stale replica; incomplete replay; hidden dependency down; undercapacity; recurring trigger; invalid backup; monitor shares fault.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Exhaustive post-recovery validation can delay urgent service; checks must be risk- and time-proportionate.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Repair completion evolved from component-up to state-, dependency-, consumer- and mission-valid restoration.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A recovery case with explicit preconditions, authoritative state, functional/data/dependency postconditions, independent validation and fallback.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A closed incident or successful command is not the property; observed re-establishment of required function is.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: GitLab lost data despite recovery work; AWS performed integrity safety checks before full service; Meta staged restoration under load (SRC-058–SRC-060).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: For truly stateless/idempotent components, simple restart may be a valid cheap path—but that must be established, not assumed.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What independent postcondition set is sufficient for complex services without making RTO unattainable?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Backup, restore and reconstitution paths must be exercised and validated
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Data backup/contingency practice, disaster recovery and current NIST restore/reconstitution guidance.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Maintain a backup copy and a recovery plan.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Copies can be absent, stale, corrupt, inaccessible, incompatible, contaminated or impossible to restore within field constraints.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Restore required data/state and application function to a trusted, current-enough configuration within RPO/RTO and consequence limits.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Backup job reports success but restore cannot complete, recovered data is inconsistent, required tools/docs are unavailable or the same cause contaminates sources.
properties.MECHANISM: Inventory sources, isolate/protect them, verify integrity/freshness, rehearse non-production restore, validate application semantics and reconstitution logistics.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any claim of backup, disaster recovery, spare image, replicated state, rebuild-from-code or clean-room recovery.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For reproducible stateless artefacts, verify rebuild and one functional check instead of elaborate backup infrastructure.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Configuration manifests, credentials, tools, dependencies, capacity, state consistency, acceptance criteria and staff capability.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Converts backup existence into demonstrated recoverability and exposes hidden RPO/RTO/support gaps.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Service/data owner, operator, mission continuity authority and affected users.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Silent backup failure; restore never tested; missing encryption key; version mismatch; partial database; dependent identity/DNS unavailable; contaminated image.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Frequent full rehearsals are costly and can create production risk; representative, isolated exercises and cheaper checks should be chosen by decision value.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Backup media inventory evolved toward recurring restore, application/state validation, clean reconstitution and dependency/tool readiness.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A periodically refreshed restore/reconstitution demonstration closing on functional and state postconditions for the current configuration.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A backup icon, policy or DR document is not the property; a valid exercised recovery path is.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: GitLab’s periodic backups were not working and snapshots were unavailable; data could not be fully recovered (SRC-060).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: A single successful restore does not establish all future restores, configurations or correlated disaster conditions.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can restore evidence be maintained continuously for large stateful systems without prohibitive duplication?

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.COVERAGE: Claim coverage is limited to tested/observed failure modes, environments and paths.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Service/data owner, operator, mission continuity authority and affected users.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: For reproducible stateless artefacts, verify rebuild and one functional check instead of elaborate backup infrastructure.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: A single successful restore does not establish all future restores, configurations or correlated disaster conditions.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS: Evidence expires when configuration, profile, environment, support organisation or dependencies materially change.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: A periodically refreshed restore/reconstitution demonstration closing on functional and state postconditions for the current configuration.

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Conditional validity of retry, restart, rollback and checkpoint recovery
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Recovery blocks, checkpoint/restart, transaction rollback and high-availability operations.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Retry a failed operation, restart the process, roll back the version or resume from a checkpoint.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Recovery primitives are beneficial for transient/local faults but amplify overload, repeat deterministic faults or restore inconsistent state when assumptions fail.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Complete the intended operation or restore service/state without duplicate side effects, overload, corruption or recurrence.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Retry storm, non-idempotent duplicate, domino rollback, stale checkpoint, incompatible rollback, restart loop or hidden dependency failure.
properties.MECHANISM: Classify fault transience; bound retries/backoff; establish idempotency; coordinate checkpoints; validate rollback compatibility; circuit-break and escalate.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Transient faults, process crashes, failed releases or recoverable state loss where operation semantics and state are known.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Do not retry deterministic validation errors or overload; fail clearly and preserve evidence.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Idempotency/deduplication, state consistency, checkpoint freshness, dependency capacity, rollback artefacts and stop conditions.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: Credible failure-domain independence, common-cause analysis, standby condition, switchover coverage and state compatibility.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Shortens restoration for the subset of failures these primitives actually cover.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Service owner, operator, recovery controller and users.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Retries increase load; checkpoint overhead; uncoordinated state; old schema cannot roll back; automated loop destroys evidence.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Recovery primitives can mask design defects and create correlated cascades; their success rate is workload- and fault-specific.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Unconditional restart evolved toward bounded, idempotent, state-aware recovery with escalation and postcondition validation.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A fault-class-specific recovery policy with bounded attempts, consistency/compatibility proof, load protection, observation and fallback.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A restart button, retry library or checkpoint file is not the property; valid semantics and successful postconditions are.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: AWS accumulated backlogs and staged recovery; Meta avoided all-at-once restart; GitLab’s restore source was incomplete (SRC-058–SRC-060).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: For independent transient faults in stateless/idempotent operations, retry/restart has strong practical value.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should automated recovery estimate when a fault is transient versus systematic under sparse evidence?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Repairability and maintainability by design
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Post-war maintainability programmes, maintainability prediction/demonstration and modular field replacement.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Reduce mean corrective maintenance time through modularity, accessibility and standard repair tasks.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A reliable design can impose unacceptable downtime or recurring error because faults cannot be isolated, accessed, repaired or verified in the field.
properties.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Restore the defined function safely within the total downtime bound under actual field support conditions.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Procedure exists but access, isolation, tools, spares, skills, state/configuration transfer or verification make repair infeasible or error-prone.
properties.MECHANISM: Design for access, isolation, modular replacement, test points, diagnostics, standard interfaces, safe handling, configuration/state transfer and repair verification.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Repairable/high-value/long-life systems, remote sites, tight restoration bounds, repeated service intervention or obsolescence exposure.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low-cost short-life items, replacement or graceful discard may dominate elaborate repairability.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Maintenance concept, field observations, human factors, logistics, tools, documentation, configuration control and testability.
properties.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
properties.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
properties.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
properties.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.
properties.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.
properties.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces active repair and error while making reliability growth and lifecycle support feasible.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Maintainer, operator, logistics owner, asset owner and service user.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Modularity moves complexity to interfaces; inaccessible fasteners; ambiguous connectors; replacement loses calibration/state; “no fault found.”
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Optimising predicted MTTR can ignore diagnosis, logistics and validation; modularity can add failure points.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Task-time prediction evolved toward maintainability-by-design, testability, software operability, remote support and total restoration burden.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Field-demonstrated restoration capability spanning detection, access, repair/replacement, configuration/state preservation, validation and return to service.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A maintainability prediction is not the property; repair performed correctly under real support constraints is.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Meta’s need for physical onsite access and GitLab’s undocumented/manual repair path show design and organisational support dominate restoration (SRC-059, SRC-060).
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: For disposable or non-repairable items, maintainability may not trigger; replacement/logistics still require analysis.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can software state/configuration portability be treated as a first-class maintainability attribute across generations?
